### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cloud-connection/package.json`, `packages/cloud-connection/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**47** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a2240c4dcfc3a19f058cb0b3a4f15a351908acde`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cloud-connection/package.json`, `packages/cloud-connection/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a2240c4dcfc3a19f058cb0b3a4f15a351908acde` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f1694e51a053e436e3b209aaaac3da6e28a34def` — the merge of head `944ebdb98d6e53c7882c614705141d7ac776edf6` into base `a2240c4dcfc3a19f058cb0b3a4f15a351908acde`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f1694e51a053e436e3b209aaaac3da6e28a34def && git checkout f1694e51a053e436e3b209aaaac3da6e28a34def
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a2240c4dcfc3a19f058cb0b3a4f15a351908acde 944ebdb98d6e53c7882c614705141d7ac776edf6 && git checkout -B drift-repro a2240c4dcfc3a19f058cb0b3a4f15a351908acde && git merge --no-ff 944ebdb98d6e53c7882c614705141d7ac776edf6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a2240c4dcfc3a19f058cb0b3a4f15a351908acde
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a2240c4dcfc3a19f058cb0b3a4f15a351908acde` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Full record on this PR (stage W2 of #15204, the walled catalog refusal at the package doors, ADR-0131 D3). Reviewed read-only: the PR body, its 13-file list (+650 / −14), the net diff of `b7e2eaf5f0` against `main` (merge base `e4ad6776d1`; `main` read at `1bd612bd68`, one commit past the base, touching none of the PR's paths), the delta `0d0a42082d..b7e2eaf5f0` (one docs commit, 2 files, +8 / −2), card #15204's body and all 162 comments through the dev's addendum 6117573171 (among them the W2 seat note 6114823168, the 17.7.0 measurement 6114989076, the stage-W seat note 6113841670, the stage-W contract review 6115069587, the Landed record 6117358377, the next-prerelease ruling 6117174845 and its addendum 6117531327), ADR-0131 D3 and D6 and ADR-0087 (the launch-window section and the disposition vocabulary) as served on `main`, and on `main`: `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` and its siblings (`meta-write-capability.ts`), `readEffectiveTenancyPosture` and `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture`, every branch of `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`, the whole install-local plugin, `security-catalog-namespace.ts` and the registry's `packageHeldSecurityCatalogNames`, `protocol.ts`'s `deletePackage`, `installPackage`, `publishPackageDrafts`, `revertStoredPackage`, `revertCommit`, `rollbackToPackageCommit` and `duplicatePackage`, `PackageInstallBodySchema` and `ManifestSchema`, the `cloud-connection-plugin.ts` install proxy, the migration-entries README, and the headers of `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`. Nothing was built, run, re-run or ablated.

**Gate verdicts on the head, read 2026-10-12T04:19Z.** 33 check-runs: 23 `completed` — 21 `success`, 2 `skipped` (the roster skips `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`) — and **10 still `in_progress`, named here as pending: `Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3)`, `Dogfood Regression Gate (3/3)`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`, `Test Core (5/6)`, `Test Core (6/6)`, `Type Check · workspace`**; their conclusions are the gate verdicts when they land, and this record does not pre-empt them. Green among the completed: `Auto Label`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Check Changeset`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3)`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`, `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `Spec property liveness`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Validate Package Dependencies`, `filter`. Where a judgment below says "pinned", the pin is one of the green runs above — the dogfood shards carry `wall-package-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` (19 pins) beside W's `wall-catalog-refusal` (17), `Lint & Repo Gates` carries `check:system-context-census` and `check:test-source-alias`, `Type Check · source gates` carries `@objectstack/spec`'s `check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide` and `check:docs` (the gates that read the new entry), `Check Changeset` carries `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, and `Test Core` carries the `spec` migration suites and the `cloud-connection`, `objectql` and `runtime` suites — not a local run. The PR is a draft, `mergeable` true, `mergeable_state` `blocked`; no review is submitted on it.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.

1. **The doors that ask the predicate (brief point a).** Three doors now ask `walledCatalogWriteVerdict` at the operator rung, after their own capability gate and before any write, and none asks a held capability:
   - `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` (install and upgrade): `refuseWalledCatalogPackage` runs after `requireInstallCapability`, the body parse, `normalizeBundle` and the id gate, and before the protocol handshake, the collision check, the posture gate, the hot-register and the ledger write. Its rung input is `authz.posture` off the admission's one `resolveAuthzContext` read; its posture input is the EFFECTIVE posture `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture` resolved for that same read. The operator control (install, upgrade, uninstall at 200 under both walled postures) pins that the operator's rung is `PLATFORM_ADMIN` through that read — **right**.
   - `DELETE /api/v1/marketplace/install-local/:id` (uninstall): the same helper, after the capability gate and the ledger `has` check, before `ledger.remove`, the registry withdrawal and the grant revocation — **right**.
   - `DELETE /api/v1/packages/:id` (`refuseWalledCatalogPackageDelete`): after `requireManageMetadata` and `requireWritablePackage`, before `resolveProtocol`, `deletePackage`, the registry withdrawal and the disable-record clear; the rung is `executionContext.posture`, the posture `readEffectiveTenancyPosture`, `isSystem` passed through — the same inputs as `meta.ts`'s dispatcher `PUT` and the clone door on `main` — **right**.
   - The predicate is asked FIRST for `SECURITY_CATALOG_TYPES[0]` and the package is read only when that answer refuses. The answer cannot vary by type (the predicate's type branch only folds the URL spelling and picks the noun), so the short-circuit is exact. The posture itself is still resolved for every admitted caller (a service resolve, not a store read), at both transports, exactly as W's clone door resolves it for every clone — **right**.
   - `PATCH /packages/:id/disable` and `/enable`: `disablePackage` / `enablePackage` flip the registry's enabled bit and `setPackageDisabled` persists the choice; no `sys_metadata` row and no registry item moves, and the dev measured B's resolution unchanged across a disable (PR body table). D3 governs creating, changing and deleting catalog items, so leaving `disable` unrefused is **right** under D3. Whether a walled organization's holder may switch an environment-wide package off at all is D6/D12's question, the same open question the PR's acceptance notes carry to the maintainer — not this stage's.
   - `POST /api/v1/packages` (the dispatcher install): `PackageInstallBodySchema` is the strict wrapped request over `ManifestSchema`, or a bare `ManifestSchema`; `ManifestSchema.permissions` is the ADR-0025 capability GRANT object (a non-array, which `declaredSecurityCatalogNames` skips by design), `capabilities` is a `retiredKey` tombstone, and there is no `positions` key; the `overwrite` path re-installs the package row through `protocolSvc.installPackage` and deletes no stored row. That door can neither add nor remove a catalog item, so the seat note's reading holds — **right** to leave it unasked.
   - `cloud-connection-plugin.ts`'s `POST …/install`: a proxy to the cloud control plane's `install_package` action with the environment's service credential; whatever the cloud does lands in this runtime through one of the doors above, so it adds no door of its own here. Its cloud-side authorization is the cloud repository's.
   - **Doors left out, by reading (not measured):** four `/packages` branches behind `requireManageMetadata` (no rung) reach `sys_metadata` rows bound to a writable package with no type filter and no walled check anywhere in their chain (`metadata-protocol` carries no reference to the predicate on `main`): `POST /packages/:id/publish-drafts` promotes every pending draft of the package, a `position` / `permission` draft included; `POST /packages/:id/commits/:commitId/revert` and `POST /packages/:id/rollback` restore or soft-remove a commit's artifacts whatever their type; `POST /packages/:id/duplicate` copies every non-object row of a base into a new package, catalog rows included. Each needs an operator-authored draft, commit or stored catalog row in a writable package first (under W a tenant can no longer author one), and each is outside ruling 6114823168's letter (install-local, and the `/packages` delete). `revert` and `discard-drafts` only discard drafts (`revertStoredPackage` reads the published rows solely to answer the 409) and `adopt-orphans` re-binds `package_id` without touching a definition, so none of those three changes what an organization resolves. Carried to ③ item 2 as an escalation; the PR's texts claim nothing about these doors.

2. **"Catalog-carrying package (whole package)" (brief point b).** The install-local doors read three sources through the engine's own reading: the incoming manifest (after `normalizeBundle`, so a compiled bundle's sections are read), the installed manifest from the ledger (`InstalledManifestEntry.manifest`, the full artifact `handleInstall` wrote), and the running registry's held position and permission-set names under the id (`findPackageHeldSecurityCatalogNames`, which covers a package the ledger does not hold). `declaredSecurityCatalogNames` is the function `registry.ts` itself registers from (`:2452`, `:2475`): the `positions`, `permissions` and `capabilities` arrays, plus each nested `plugins[]` entry's, names by `name` else `id`. The `/packages` delete reads the stored `sys_metadata` rows with that `package_id`, the type folded through `isSecurityCatalogType`, through the same unpaginated `find` `deletePackage` reads them with (`protocol.ts:23822`), so the door refuses on exactly the population the delete would remove; a failed read answers through `errorFromThrown`, never an admit. The refusal is one answer for the whole package before any step, and a catalog-free package stays installable, upgradable, uninstallable and deletable by the same tenant (the CONTROL pins under both walled postures; `declared.length === 0` and `storedTypes.size === 0` admit). A catalog-free incoming version over an installed catalog-carrying one is refused (the ruling's "either version"), pinned — **right**, all of it.

3. **Envelope (brief point c).** install-local answers `403` `FORBIDDEN`, the code `requireInstallCapability`'s own refusal uses in this plugin, with `details.catalogItems` and the predicate's message (which names the posture and the `manage_metadata` capability, as D3 asks); the dispatcher answers `deps.error(…, 403)`, this transport's `PERMISSION_DENIED`. That is the split stage W fixed on `main`: `FORBIDDEN` at the REST doors, `PERMISSION_DENIED` at the dispatcher `PUT`, the clone door and the data door — **consistent**. The pins assert status and code together and the posture in the message.

4. **Controls (brief point d).** `single`: the predicate admits on `!postureEnforcesWall`, and the dogfood `single` control has the same sub-operator `manage_metadata` holder install, upgrade, uninstall and delete catalog-carrying packages at 200 — unchanged. The operator: admitted on the `PLATFORM_ADMIN` rung, pinned on its own packages. No `tenancy` service: `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture` and `readEffectiveTenancyPosture` both answer `undefined` for a never-registered service, which the predicate admits — inert. A registered `tenancy` service that cannot answer: install-local's admission re-raises the branded `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` (pre-existing since the posture became an admission input; untouched here); the dispatcher's `readEffectiveTenancyPosture` throws the same brand, which `handlePackagesRequest`'s outer catch hands to `errorFromThrown`, and `resolveThrownHttpError` reads the error's own `status` 503 (`SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`). Refused, never admitted, on both transports — **as stage W does**. One consequence worth naming: because the posture is read before the catalog read, that outage now refuses every `DELETE /packages/:id` that passes the capability and writable gates, a catalog-free delete under `single` included — the activation gate's and W's shape ("the posture is an authorization input and was never decided"), not a defect.

5. **The spec entry and the changeset (brief point e).**
   - `18.walled-catalog-package-writes-retired.ts`: the semantic shape the entries README prescribes (`id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`), under the protocol major the file prefix names, beside W's `18.walled-catalog-tenant-writes-retired.ts`; the directory is concatenated into the git-ignored `registry.ts` by `gen:migration-registry`, so there is no index to edit — W landed with the same two-file footprint. `surface` carries no backticks; it names the three doors exactly as the code refuses them, the "incoming version, or installed version on an upgrade" clause included. `replacement`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` read as the code behaves (403 `FORBIDDEN` / 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, the posture in the message, the catalog-free and `single` controls) — **right**.
   - The changeset: `minor` for `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec` — the four published packages whose source the diff moves. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on its own line, the `**BREAKING**` banner, and the ADR-0087 marker `registered walled-catalog-package-writes-retired` in an HTML comment, naming an id that resolves and is new in the diff. The FROM → TO bullets: the install-local install/upgrade bullet, the uninstall bullet and the `/packages` delete bullet each read against the door above — **right**; the delete bullet says "positions or permission sets" where the code also counts a stored `capability` row, a code-only type that no door stores outside the `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE` escape hatch (text, ③ item 4). The "Unchanged" paragraph (catalog-free packages, the operator, `single`, no `tenancy` service, `disable`) and the remedy (the operator does it; the entry id; the predicate asked once per declared type; the new export) are exact.

6. **The `@objectstack/objectql` export and the `cloud-connection` dependency (brief point f).** `declaredSecurityCatalogNames` and the type `DeclaredSecurityCatalogName` join the package's root export beside the already-exported `findPackageHeldSecurityCatalogNames`: an additive public-surface widening, which the changeset names in its remedy paragraph under `@objectstack/objectql: minor`; `objectql` keeps no api-surface snapshot (only `spec` does), so no artifact is owed — **right**. `@objectstack/objectql: workspace:*` is added to `cloud-connection`'s `dependencies` with its lockfile importer row; `objectql` depends on `core`, `formula`, `metadata`, `metadata-core`, `metadata-protocol`, `spec` and `types`, never on `cloud-connection`, and `runtime` (already a `cloud-connection` dependency) already depends on `objectql`, so the edge adds no cycle and inverts no layer — the closure claim in the body is true. `Validate Package Dependencies` (lockfile currency, the fixed group, override consistency) is green on this head. The `vitest.config.ts` alias makes the package's suites read this checkout's `objectql/src`, the `check:test-source-alias` fix the body reports — **right**.

7. **Census row 55b, the counts, and the prose (brief point g).** Row 55b adds `runtime` to its package column, the `/packages` delete of a package holding stored positions or permission sets to its door list, and the anchor `packages.ts#refuseWalledCatalogPackageDelete`. Against the code: the row's bypass is the `ec?.isSystem === true` read handed to the predicate — one new `ExecutionContext.isSystem` read, in one new symbol, behaviour-bearing — so 130 → 131 reads, 127 → 128 behaviour-bearing, 135 → 136 property reads and 110 → 111 anchored symbols, with the `context: { isSystem: true }` of the row read being a producer-side literal (the dated object-literal row, unchanged) and the install-local plugin adding no `isSystem` read at all — **consistent**. `capabilities.mdx`'s new paragraph: on `main` the REST `walledCatalogRefusal` runs before `resolveProtocol` and answers `FORBIDDEN`, the dispatcher `PUT` answers `PERMISSION_DENIED`, both `403`, and under `single` (and with no `tenancy` service) the predicate is inert so the code-only `NOT_CREATABLE` block is what every caller reads — exactly the clause 6115069587 ③ 3 ii asked for — **right**. `system-context.mdx`'s three prose counts move with the table.

8. **The delta on this head (two docs edits, read sentence by sentence).** `metadata-api.mdx`, `DELETE /packages/:id`: "Under a `group` or `isolated` tenancy posture, a package holding positions or permission sets is the platform operator's to delete: any other caller is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` (ADR-0131 D3)." Exact for a writable package, the only kind this door deletes; a code or installed package holding them answers `422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` to every caller first, which the section never mentioned before either (text, ③ item 4). `permission-sets.mdx`, the provenance paragraph: "removing a package that carries positions or permission sets is the platform operator's (ADR-0131 D3): that delete, and an `install-local` install, upgrade or uninstall of such a package, refuse any other caller `403` before anything changes." Each door refuses before its first write (item 1), and the sentence names only the status, which both transports share — **right**.

### ② Semver level

- The diff publishes an accept-set narrowing at three doors (BREAKING, shipped `minor` under ADR-0087's launch-window rule, which `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces), an additive export in `@objectstack/objectql`, a new dependency edge in `@objectstack/cloud-connection`'s published manifest, and in `@objectstack/spec` one semantic entry. The changeset grades exactly those four packages `minor`, carries the banner, the `registered` marker and `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; the PR body carries the same line on its third line, after `Part of #15204` and a blank line, the placement 6115069587 accepted for W. **The level matches what the diff publishes, and so does the Clause-② line.** `Check Changeset` (the ADR-0087 registration gate against the merge base, the no-major guard and the level-axis reader) is green on this head.
- Packages touched without a changeset: `@objectstack/qa/dogfood` (private) and `content/docs` — owe none. `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `cloud-connection/vitest.config.ts` publish nothing.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry, answered or escalated.

1. **The dev's addendum 6117573171** (head `b7e2eaf5f0`, `open_questions: []`): its two deviations are accepted. (i) The branch carries W's original commits beneath the merge of `main`: verified — the net diff against the merge base holds exactly the 13 files of the PR's own list and no hunk of W's (W's changes sit on `main` beneath the merge base, and the two pages both stages touch, `system-context.mdx` and `permission-sets.mdx`, carry only W2's lines in this diff), and `main` has moved one commit since, touching none of these paths. (ii) The scope beyond the dispatch's letter is the ruling's own: 6114823168 asked for the `/packages` delete to be measured and refused if reachable, the `disable` measurement is a control, and the two docs pages follow the drift comment. Its one `out_of_scope_findings` entry (dispatch-gates derived no `cloud-connection` unit-test command for a `cloud-connection/src` change) is tooling, noted and not filed; the seat decides whether to file it. One slip in the addendum's prose: it says the census anchors "130 sites" while the diff moves the page to 131; the diff is right.
2. **Escalated to the seat, not a condition of this verdict: the four `/packages` doors of ① item 1.** `publish-drafts`, `commits/:commitId/revert`, `rollback` and `duplicate` can, by reading, promote, restore, remove or copy a catalog row bound to a writable package behind `requireManageMetadata` alone, under a wall, once the operator has authored such a draft, commit or row. Ruling 6114823168 named install-local and the `/packages` delete, the W2 measurement did not reach these, and the PR's changeset, entry, census row and docs claim nothing about them — so this PR is exact about what it closes and these are not its to close, the way 6115069587 ① 6 placed the package door outside stage W. They want a measurement and a ruling before release-cut condition (f) is read as "every door" rather than "the measured doors".
3. **Carried, unchanged:** whether a walled organization's `manage_metadata` may install packages at all, or author the environment's objects, views and flows (the PR's acceptance notes; 6114823168 "Not decided here"; 6113841670 "Carried, not filed"). The maintainer's.
4. **For the seat, text only:** (i) `metadata-api.mdx`'s "a package holding positions or permission sets is the platform operator's to delete" — for a read-only package nobody deletes it over this API (`422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` first); "a writable package" would be exact. (ii) The changeset's delete bullet and the census row say "positions or permission sets" while the code refuses on any stored security-catalog type; no door stores a `capability` row, so the accept set is the same. (iii) The install-local docblock's "nothing is read" for an admitted caller: the ledger entry is read before the predicate at both doors (a local JSON read; no store, no registry), which is what the body's "neither door reads anything new" means. None moves the accept set or the level.
5. **Local-runs: none.** No worktree, build, test, gate or ablation was run; the scratch space `pr-22935/` holds only this round's reads. The dev's ablation and full-suite numbers are read as reported, not re-measured; the pins are the gate runs named above.
6. **Size and tier.** 13 files, +650 / −14: not governed (no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`), far under the 3,000-line class. `Part of #15204`, no closing keyword, assignee set, draft, `mergeable` true, `mergeable_state` `blocked`. No review is submitted on the PR. ⛔ Not armed, not approved, not readied by this review; the seat's pre-landing check and the queue follow.
